dimensions.name: Requirements clarification
dimensions.description: Identifies functional and non-functional requirements before drawing.

levels.1: Jumps to components without clarifying requirements.
levels.2: Lists requirements only after prompting, or misses key constraints.
levels.3: Clarifies the main requirements and states reasonable assumptions.
levels.4: Prioritizes requirements, resolves ambiguity, and records explicit assumptions.

dimensions.name: Back-of-envelope estimation
dimensions.description: Quantifies traffic, storage, and bandwidth to justify design choices.

levels.1: No estimates or estimates that are off by orders of magnitude.
levels.2: Provides partial estimates with unclear assumptions.
levels.3: Produces reasonable estimates for traffic, storage, and read/write ratio.
levels.4: Uses estimates to drive design decisions and checks them for consistency.

dimensions.name: API and data model
dimensions.description: Defines the core API and the persisted entities and relationships.

levels.1: No usable API or data model.
levels.2: Sketchy API or model with missing key fields or relationships.
levels.3: Defines the main endpoints and entities with sensible keys and indexes.
levels.4: Explains API contracts, schema choices, indexes, and evolution strategy.

dimensions.name: High-level architecture
dimensions.description: Shows components, boundaries, and the main request/data flow.

levels.2: Shows components but not how requests or data move between them.
levels.3: Shows a coherent architecture and explains the main flows.
levels.4: Makes boundaries and failure domains explicit and justifies the shape.

dimensions.name: Deep dives
dimensions.description: Explores the hard parts of the chosen design in detail.

levels.1: No deep dive, or a deep dive unrelated to the requirements.
levels.2: Mentions a hard problem but stays at a high level.
levels.3: Explains at least one critical mechanism such as partitioning, caching, or consistency.
levels.4: Explains mechanisms, failure behavior, and the trade-offs between alternatives.

dimensions.name: Trade-offs
dimensions.description: Compares alternatives and explains why the chosen design fits.

levels.2: Lists alternatives without connecting them to requirements.
levels.3: Compares meaningful alternatives and justifies the choice.
levels.4: Quantifies trade-offs and explains when the decision would change.

dimensions.name: Communication
dimensions.description: Explains the design clearly and keeps the discussion structured.

levels.2: Understandable but unstructured or missing context.
levels.3: Clear structure, defined terms, and a coherent narrative.
levels.4: Adapts depth to the audience, summarizes decisions, and handles questions precisely.
